pairs.subject: background-jobs
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:46 The scheduler derives one interval from configuration and sleeps that long after every pass, so how fast it notices due work never changes with whether anything is in flight.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/storage.rs:1824 The pass pulse upserts only a timestamp. There is no owner identity, claim-before-run, or verify-before-fire, so a second process is not stood down. Stop itself is present: the loop watches the shared token and main joins the task for SCHEDULER_SHUTDOWN_GRACE.

crates/server/src/main.rs:79 Panic is caught around the tick and around each schedule, and the loop continues; the e2e test pins that. There is still no per-tick deadline in steady state and no consecutive-failure quarantine — the only bound is the shutdown grace.

crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:110 Fixed-delay sleep of the same interval after every pass. No idle rate, no jitter, and no wake when a schedule is created; notify_one wakes the worker after enqueue, not this loop.

crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:246 Silence is real: pass_is_stale uses schedule_tick_secs × 4 (floor 60s), None is stale, and GET /schedules reads the heartbeat from outside the loop. An all-idle pass is not a recorded succeeded-empty outcome, and crash, timeout, and skipped are not tick-exit marks.

crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:574 The first pass shares decide() with steady state. last_pass None uses the grace floor; fire_once collapses to one run; skip enumeration stops at MAX_MISFIRE_SCAN; the ledger labels a collapsed catch-up.

crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:3 This loop admits a queue job and returns. scheduler.rs has no progress, phase, or ETA writes. Cancel hits are the shutdown token and treating job status cancelled as slot-free, not a cancelling state.
crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:590 The step reports that it enqueued. It does not hold a job handle or give up a bounded wait, and there is no forever-budget sentinel in this file.

pairs.registryProposal: The golden path sends missed-run policy to scheduling, but this loop's body is the recurrence engine. Say which host clauses still bind in that fusion — cadence, per-tick deadline, tick-outcome vocabulary, single-runner claim — so a scheduler file is not scored as pure policy and not as if it owned job progress.
